inspector.rule1: Rows marked “Cleanable” can be cleaned from the inspector (moved to the Trash); repositories with build artifacts can clean only the artifacts (node_modules / target, etc.), keeping the source code.
inspector.rule2: Toolchain cache rows that have an official cleanup command are not marked “Cleanable” — the command is shown in Details. Run it yourself; it is more precise than moving the whole folder.
inspector.rule3: Editor and AI tools are cleaned by “tool × category” (logs / sessions / caches); sessions contain the full conversation history and are not regenerated after deletion.
inspector.readOnly: This group is read-only: a reclaimable figure doesn't mean there is a delete action.
clean.title: Move to Trash
clean.repoBody: The entire repository folder (including source code and .git history) will be moved to the Trash. You can restore it from the Trash later.
clean.aiBody: The {kind} entry under “{name}” will be moved to the Trash. You can restore it from the Trash later.
clean.sessionStrong: Sessions contain the full conversation history and code snippets; deleting them is not automatically reversed.
clean.sessionAfter: Logs and caches regenerate the next time the tool runs.
clean.otherAfter: Logs and caches regenerate on the next run; features are unaffected.
clean.cacheBody: The entire cache folder will be moved to the Trash. You can restore it from the Trash later; it will be downloaded or rebuilt when next needed, and features are unaffected.
clean.repoReview: Repositories with unpushed commits or uncommitted changes are rejected — state may have changed since the scan, so the server rechecks every item.
clean.aiReview: The server confirms the tool is still on the scan allowlist and reclassifies files as of the click; only top-level entries still in this category are cleaned. Deleted sessions can only be recovered from the Trash.
clean.cacheReview: If a build or download is running, wait for it to finish.
clean.recheckWhitelist: The server rechecks that this item is still on the cleanable allowlist.
clean.estimate: Reclaimable is an estimate: folders with shared hard links (such as Rust's target/) may be overstated.
clean.batchRepoBody.one: The following {count} repository (including source code and .git history) will be moved to the Trash. You can restore it from the Trash later.
clean.batchRepoBody.other: The following {count} repositories (including source code and .git history) will be moved to the Trash. You can restore them from the Trash later.
clean.batchAiBody.one: The following {count} “tool × category” entry will be moved to the Trash. You can restore it from the Trash later.
clean.batchAiBody.other: The following {count} “tool × category” entries will be moved to the Trash. You can restore them from the Trash later.
clean.batchCacheBody.one: The following {count} cache folder will be moved to the Trash. You can restore it from the Trash later.
clean.batchCacheBody.other: The following {count} cache folders will be moved to the Trash. You can restore them from the Trash later.
clean.repoReviewBatch: Repositories with unpushed commits or uncommitted changes are rejected; the server checks every item and moves the rest to the Trash.
clean.aiReviewBatch: The server confirms each tool is still on the scan allowlist and reclassifies files as of the click; items that fail are listed separately and the rest move to the Trash.
clean.sessionTrash: Deleted sessions can only be recovered from the Trash.
clean.cacheReviewBatch: If a build or download is running, wait for it to finish. The server rechecks that every item is still on the cleanable allowlist; items that fail are listed separately and the rest move to the Trash.
clean.artifact.title: Clean build artifacts
clean.artifact.body.one: The selected {count} build-artifact folder will be moved to the Trash. Source code and .git are untouched; it regenerates on the next build or dependency install.
clean.artifact.body.other: The {count} selected build-artifact folders will be moved to the Trash. Source code and .git are untouched; they regenerate on the next build or dependency install.
clean.artifact.review: Unpushed commits and uncommitted changes are not checked — cleaning artifacts never touches source code. The server rediscovers artifact folders from the allowlist as of the click; artifact folders containing a Git repository are rejected.
clean.artifact.estimate: Selected size is an estimate: folders with shared hard links may be overstated.
tagHint.stale: No commits for more than 180 days
tagHint.unpushed: Has unpushed commits, or the push state couldn't be verified (no upstream / detached HEAD / git failure). Unverifiable states count as unpushed, and deleting the whole repository is refused
tagHint.modified: The working tree has uncommitted changes; deleting the whole repository is refused
tagHint.stashed: git stash is not empty. The stash lives inside .git, so moving the repository to the Trash would remove it too
tagHint.nested: Lives inside another repository folder; its size is already subtracted from the parent repository and is not counted twice
tagHint.artifacts: Contains build-artifact folders such as node_modules / target / dist; they can be cleaned separately without touching source code
tagHint.cleanable: Has a delete action: moved to the Trash, restorable from there
settings.title: Settings
settings.language.heading: Language
settings.language.hint: Changes apply immediately; no restart needed. System languages other than English, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese fall back to English.
settings.appearance.heading: Appearance
settings.appearance.hint: “Automatic” follows the system appearance; choosing Light or Dark pins it.
settings.repoRoots.heading: Git repository scan folders
settings.repoRoots.hint: Add parent folders that contain repositories. Adding or removing only refreshes Git repositories.
settings.repoRoots.removeHint: Only stops scanning; files are not deleted
settings.repoRoots.removeAria: Stop scanning {path}; files are not deleted
settings.repoRoots.footnote: Removing a folder only stops scanning it; no folders or files are deleted.
settings.cache.heading: Cache
settings.cache.hint: Scan results are cached on this machine and load instantly on launch. A real scan runs only on first launch, after the cache is cleared, or when the oldest group in the cache is more than 24 hours old.
settings.cache.autoLabel: Rescan on launch when the cache is older than 24 hours
settings.cache.autoHint: The cached data appears first, then a background rescan runs (about 26 seconds) while you keep browsing. Turn this off to update only on first launch or manual rescans.
settings.cache.clearedHint: Choose Rescan now below to start scanning, or restart the app to scan automatically.
settings.cache.footnote: A full scan takes about 26 seconds (measurement source: README “Scanning strategy”). Clearing the cache deletes no asset data; it only forces a fresh scan on the next launch.
settings.cache.clearedToast: Cache cleared · choose Rescan now below to refresh
settings.update.heading: Updates
settings.update.hint: Current version v{version}. When a new version is available, choose Download to get the installer for this platform. Downloads stay in the app and nothing installs silently: the installer opens automatically, and the final decision stays with you.
settings.update.footnoteBefore: The installer is saved to your Downloads folder and opened automatically. Neither checking nor downloading goes through a browser: checking requests only api.github.com, and the installer comes directly from GitHub release assets — no local data is sent. settings.project.hint: Stacktake is open source under the MIT license; the source, issues and license text are on GitHub. These links open in your system browser; the app makes no extra requests.

data.note.reposNoHome: Could not locate the home directory, so the scan roots can't be inferred
data.note.reposNested: {count} nested repositories detected; a parent's size excludes its nested ones
data.note.aiTools.scope: Only the whitelisted AI tool and editor data directories are scanned (see the SPECS table in ai_tools.rs); missing ones are skipped. The home directory is never searched and no file content is read
data.note.aiTools.noContent: Only file names and sizes are measured — no file content is read, so credentials never enter the scan result
data.note.aiTools.session: Session data holds complete transcripts and code snippets — deleting it is irreversible, so decide what to keep first
data.note.aiTools.index: Index categories include SQLite database files (Codex's logs_2.sqlite is named a log but is a database) — deleting them directly can corrupt the tool's state
data.note.aiTools.skill: Skills and plugins have to be reinstalled after deletion, so cleaning is not offered for them
data.note.aiTools.unknown: {count} unrecognised entries (total {bytes}) are grouped as Unknown — none of them can be cleaned
data.note.aiTools.symlinks: {count} symlinks were skipped and never followed
data.note.toolchain.noContent: Only file names and sizes are measured — no file content is read
data.note.toolchain.reclaimRule: Reclaimable means a pure download or dependency cache with no official cleanup command: deleting it only costs a re-download or rebuild. Where an official command exists you run it yourself (see each row's cleanup method) — this tool does not run it and does not count it as reclaimable
data.note.toolchain.installedNotReclaima: Installed toolchains and binaries are never reclaimable — which versions you keep is a deliberate choice
data.note.toolchain.waitBuilds: Cleanup follows each tool's official command; if a build or download is running, wait for it to finish first
data.note.toolchain.xcodeArchives: Xcode Archives are shipped builds, not caches, and are never reclaimable; a deleted simulator runtime has to be re-downloaded (official command in the details)
data.note.toolchain.versionManagers: Version managers ({managers}) list one row per installed version: keeping several is deliberate, none are reclaimable, and each uninstalls with its own command
data.note.toolchain.versionManagersNotRe: Version managers never report a reclaimable amount: this tool cannot tell which project uses which version (that would mean reading every repository's .nvmrc / engines and intersecting them), and a number here would get a still-used version deleted
data.note.toolchain.empty: None of the whitelisted cache directories exist; the matching tools may not be installed
data.note.devEnv.noContent: Only file names and sizes are measured — no file content is read
data.note.devEnv.allMissing: None of the {count} locations above exist; this environment may not be installed
data.note.java.mavenRebuildable: The Maven dependency cache can be rebuilt from the network, but deleting it means re-downloading, so it is not counted as reclaimable
data.note.java.multipleJdks: Several JDKs side by side isn't leftover here: 17 and 21 are both mainstream LTS releases and projects need different ones — which to keep is your choice
data.note.java.gradleOlder: Old Gradle distributions and daemon logs are marked reclaimable; until cleaning is enabled here they are only shown, never deleted
data.note.localModels.assetNotCache: Models are assets, not caches: deleting one means re-downloading tens of gigabytes, so this group never marks anything reclaimable
data.note.localModels.ollamaLayers: Ollama resolves the weight layers each model references through its manifest; when a layer file is missing only what's on disk is counted, and the missing count is in the details
data.note.localModels.sharedLayers: When a model has several tags its size is counted once per reference; what deleting a single tag actually frees is in the shared-layers row of the details (only shown when layers really are shared)
data.note.localModels.lmstudioScope: LM Studio scans only models/ and hub/models/ — the session, log and credential directories under ~/.lmstudio aren't model assets and are not listed
data.note.localModels.huggingfaceScope: HuggingFace is measured per model directory (snapshots are symlinks into blobs, so nothing is double-counted)
data.note.wsl.sizeMeaning: The size is the space taken by the ext4.vhdx file, not how much the distro actually uses
data.note.wsl.growsOnly: A dynamically expanding vhdx only grows: deleting files inside the distro leaves holes in the virtual disk while the file on the Windows side doesn't shrink — which is why no reclaimable number can be given here
data.note.wsl.howToShrink: Handing the space back to Windows takes three steps: sudo fstrim -av inside the distro, then wsl --shutdown, then Optimize-VHD -Mode Full (or diskpart's compact vdisk) as administrator. This tool does none of them
data.note.wsl.gapIsNormal: How big the gap can be is normal: one measured vhdx held 12 GB of data inside a 60 GB file, another showed 583 GB in Windows while df inside the distro reported 93 GB
data.note.wsl.registryOnly: Locations are read from the Lxss registry key (wsl --list -v doesn't give paths); no wsl command is run and the distro is never entered
data.summary.aiToolsEmpty: No AI tool or editor data directories found
data.summary.wsl: {count} entries · total {total} · a vhdx only grows, so nothing here is reclaimable
data.error.repoRootsChanged: Scan directories changed — rescan Git repositories
data.error.repoRootsRead: Could not read the extra Git repository directories: {error}
data.value.missingLayers: {n} (weight files not on disk; excluded from the size)
data.value.sharedLayers: {n} layers are shared with other models ({shared}) — deleting this model actually frees {freed}
data.value.downloadStaging: Download staging: the manifest and thumbnails may exist, the weights are incomplete
data.value.mavenRest: groupIds outside the top {top} by size
data.value.gradleDistKeep: Highest version, treated as the one in use — not counted as reclaimable
data.value.gradleDistOld: A newer distribution exists; the old one can be removed safely
data.value.gradleDaemonLogs: Gradle daemon logs; deleting them does not affect builds
data.value.gradleRegenerates: Regenerated or re-downloaded on the next build
data.value.vhdxSizeSemantics: Space occupied by the vhdx file, not what the distro actually uses: it grows on demand and never shrinks on its own
data.value.vhdxHowToShrink: Inside the distro: fstrim -av → wsl --shutdown → as admin: Optimize-VHD -Mode Full
data.cleanFail.pushUnknown: Push status could not be verified (treated as possibly unpushed)
data.cleanFail.repoMissing: The repository directory no longer exists — rescan
data.cleanFail.artifactOutsideRepo: Not an artifact directory path inside this repository
data.cleanFail.artifactRecheckFailed: Re-check failed (a Git repository is hidden inside, or it is no longer an artifact directory) — skipped
data.cleanFail.officialCommand: {short} has an official cleanup command — run it yourself: {cmd}
data.cleanFail.perChildOnly: {short} is cleaned per subdirectory (that is how it is listed) — deleting the whole directory is not offered
data.cleanFail.notInAiWhitelist: Not in the AI tool scan whitelist
data.cleanFail.readOnlyRoot: This tool directory is counted only — cleanup not offered
data.cleanFail.pathMissingSkipped: The path no longer exists — skipped
data.summary.docker: {images} images · {volumes} volumes · {total} in total · {unused} unreferenced · {reclaim} reclaimable
data.error.dockerEmpty: docker has no images and no volumes
data.note.dockerDesktopDiskIdle: The Docker Desktop data directory actually occupies {bytes} (~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker) — even when it is not running
data.note.dockerStartHint: Start Docker Desktop and click Rescan to see image and volume details
data.note.dockerInsideVm: Images and volumes live inside the Docker VM; there is no matching path on the host file system — every number comes from the docker CLI
data.note.dockerDecimalUnits: docker reports sizes in decimal units (1 GB = 10⁹ bytes) while the UI uses binary units, so the numbers here are roughly 10% smaller than in `docker system df`
data.note.dockerVirtualSize: Sizes are virtual: shared layers are counted once per image, so the rows add up to more than docker's total
data.note.dockerContainers: Plus {n} containers (writable layers {bytes} in total); containers are not itemised — their writable layers are usually a few KB
data.note.dockerDesktopDisk: The Docker Desktop data directory actually occupies {bytes} (~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker) — including the VM system and logs, so it is larger than the rows above and than the summary
data.note.dockerSkippedRows: {n} output rows had an unexpected format and were skipped
data.summary.ssh: {count} private keys · {orphans} not referenced by config
data.toolchainNote.nvmVersions: One directory per version. Remove with `nvm uninstall <version>` — deleting the directory by hand leaves stale entries in nvm's version list and aliases
data.toolchainNote.fnmVersions: One directory per version. Remove with `fnm uninstall <version>`
data.toolchainNote.voltaVersions: One directory per version. Remove with `volta uninstall node@<version>`
data.toolchainNote.pyenvVersions: One directory per version. Remove with `pyenv uninstall <version>`
data.toolchainNote.condaEnvs: Each subdirectory is a conda environment. Remove it with `conda env remove -n <name>`
data.toolchainNote.rbenvVersions: One directory per version. Remove with `rbenv uninstall <version>`
data.toolchainNote.asdfVersions: One directory per version. Remove with `asdf uninstall <language> <version>`
data.toolchainNote.npmCache: The command cleans _cacache; subdirectories such as _npx can be deleted directly and are re-downloaded on next use
data.toolchainNote.nvmDownloads: nvm's download staging for node tar.xz archives — leftovers once installed; installed versions live under versions/ and are unaffected
data.toolchainNote.pnpmStore: prune only removes packages no project references; deleting the whole store is also safe — it is rebuilt on demand
data.toolchainNote.pnpmNode: Node binaries managed by pnpm itself; commands that depend on them stop working if deleted
data.toolchainNote.nodeGyp: Node headers per version, downloaded when compiling native addons
data.toolchainNote.playwright: Multiple versions coexist because different projects download what they need; after deletion the project re-downloads on its next run
data.toolchainNote.cypress: Re-downloaded on the next run after deletion
data.toolchainNote.electron: Electron zips used for packaging; re-downloaded after deletion
data.toolchainNote.electronXdg: A second copy some tools keep per the XDG spec — same source as Library/Caches/electron
data.toolchainNote.electronBuilder: Packaging helpers such as dmg / nsis / wine; re-downloaded after deletion
data.toolchainNote.typescript: tsserver versions downloaded by editors; re-downloaded after deletion
data.toolchainNote.rustupToolchains: Installed toolchain versions — how many you keep is a deliberate choice, same rule as JDKs
data.toolchainNote.rustupDownloads: Temporary files from installs — leftovers once installed
data.toolchainNote.cargoRegistry: crates.io index and package cache; no official prune command, safe to delete — re-downloaded on the next build
data.toolchainNote.cargoGit: Checkout cache for git dependencies; re-cloned after deletion
data.toolchainNote.cargoBin: Binaries installed with cargo install — deleting them removes the commands
data.toolchainNote.goBuild: Intermediate build outputs; rebuilt after deletion — time-consuming but no data is lost
data.toolchainNote.goBin: Binaries installed with go install — deleting them removes the commands
data.toolchainNote.homebrew: Bottles and API cache; the Backup subdirectory holds old-version backups, and cleanup handles both
data.toolchainNote.versionedRuntime: Runtimes downloaded per version; re-downloaded after deletion
data.toolchainNote.vcpkg: Affected packages are rebuilt after deletion — time-consuming but no data is lost
data.toolchainNote.prisma: Downloaded query engines; re-downloaded after deletion
data.toolchainNote.deno: Remote modules and compiled outputs, re-downloaded on demand. Note that DENO_DIR also holds app data such as kv / webstorage — make sure nothing is using it before deleting
data.toolchainNote.nugetPackages: Expanded by package id + version and shared by all projects. After deletion each project re-downloads on restore; the NUGET_PACKAGES environment variable can relocate this directory
data.toolchainNote.nugetHttp: Raw downloads (.dat) not yet expanded, with a 30-minute expiry
data.toolchainNote.composer: Downloaded zips (files), repository metadata (repo) and VCS checkouts (vcs). A project's vendor/ is not in here
data.toolchainNote.coursier: Artifact cache for Scala / sbt, organised by URL. The v1 subdirectory is the version
data.toolchainNote.coursierLegacy: The coursier default location before October 2017. Whichever coursier version ran first on this machine decides which one is used; having both means an old version was once run
data.toolchainNote.swiftpm: Dependency checkouts and repository cache; re-downloaded on the next resolve. SourcePackages inside Xcode projects live under DerivedData, not here
data.toolchainNote.cocoapods: Downloaded pods; pod install fetches them again. ~/.cocoapods/repos is deliberately not scanned — it holds spec repositories that only pod repo update can restore, a different cost from the other rows
data.toolchainNote.derivedData: Each subdirectory is one project's build index and intermediates, rebuilt on the next build; wait for builds in progress to finish first
data.toolchainNote.deviceSupport: System symbols extracted from a connected device, one row per iOS version; regenerated the next time a device with that version connects
data.toolchainNote.xcodeArchives: Archives uploaded to the App Store (with dSYM symbols) — deleting loses the archive history. These are products, not caches, and are never counted as reclaimable
data.toolchainNote.simulatorRuntimes: Downloaded simulator runtimes, one row per version; re-download through Xcode after deletion. The official command deletes precisely by runtime ID — this tool does not run it
